detail.reason: Customer reports PreSense transfer data loss bug, voice agent handoff context loss, and pricing pushback on per-minute AI Voice Agent.

steps.summary: 4 candidate insights (2 bug, 1 pricing objection, 1 praise)
Joined 2 existing themes · started 2 candidate themes

assignments.name: PreSense data lost on Genesys warm transfers
AI agent handoff loses caller details
Signal AI priced as separate add-on
Campaign attribution view is daily go-to

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Morning, everyone. Thanks for making time. I know Q3 close is always busy on your side, so I'll keep us moving.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Morning, [PERSON_1]. We're good. [PERSON_2]'s dialed in from the office, [PERSON_3]'s on his headset somewhere.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'm here. Can you hear me okay?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Loud and clear. Let's start with the numbers, then I want to leave plenty of room for the stuff you flagged.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Sounds good.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So inbound sales calls for Q3 came in at about 41,200, that's up 7% over Q2. Fiber install calls were the biggest mover, roughly 12,800 of that total.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Yeah, that lines up with what we saw on the media side. The fiber campaign in the Denver metro really carried the quarter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Attribution held up well too. About 68% of those calls tied back to a paid campaign or keyword, which is a couple points better than last quarter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: The new attribution view by campaign is honestly the report my team opens first every morning.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good to hear. Anything you want changed on it, just tell me and I'll pass it along.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Not right now. It's doing what we need.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. On the AI Voice Agent side, containment came in at 31% for the quarter. That's up from 24% in Q2.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: That's a real jump. What's driving it?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Mostly the billing and hours-of-operation calls. Those are the two intents getting handled end to end without a transfer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That matches what I see in Genesys. The queue volume for general billing is down noticeably.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. And messaging, the SMS follow-up after a missed call, that's running at about 4,100 conversations for the quarter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: We've had decent pickup on that. The sales team likes it because it keeps the lead warm.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay, that's the summary. [PERSON_2], you had something on the PreSense side you wanted to walk through?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Yeah, this is the big one for me. Every time we transfer from sales to retention in Genesys, the PreSense data just doesn't come across. The second agent gets nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the screen pop works on the first leg into sales, but on the warm transfer to retention it drops.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Correct. The retention agent sees the caller ID and that's it. No journey, no pages viewed, nothing. They end up asking the customer to repeat everything.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: How often is this happening?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It's consistent. Any time the call moves from the sales skill to retention. I'd say a few hundred calls a week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. And this is the second time this quarter we've talked about transfer behavior.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: It is. I raised it in August and we didn't get to a fix.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I remember. Let me get the specifics from you after this call, the exact skill names and a couple of example calls, and I'll take it to the team.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I don't want to guess at the cause on the call.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That works. I can pull two or three call IDs this afternoon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Perfect. [PERSON_3], you had the other one.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: The voice agent is handing people to a live rep and the rep has to ask for the account number again. That's the one thing we told customers they wouldn't have to do.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So the handoff from the voice agent into the live queue isn't carrying the context over.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Right. The agent collected the account number, verified the caller, then transfers, and the rep starts from zero. It makes us look like we don't know who's calling.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Is it every handoff or specific intents?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Mostly the ones that go to the billing queue. The sales handoffs seem better, but I haven't measured it closely.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. Can you send me a few examples too? Same as [PERSON_2], call IDs and the time of day. I'll bring both of these to the product team together since they're related.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Yeah, I'll get you something by Friday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks. [PERSON_4], you mentioned procurement.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Procurement is going to ask me why AI Voice Agent is priced per minute on top of the platform fee. I need a better answer than I have.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fair. Is this for the renewal planning or a separate review?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: It's the annual vendor review. They look at every line item and they've been on a cost-per-outcome kick all year.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Got it. Let me pull the usage detail and put together something you can hand them. I'd rather give you real numbers than a talking point.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That would help. They respond better to math than to a slide.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Understood. I'll have that to you by early next week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Thanks.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Anything else on your list before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: The Google Ads and Adobe Analytics connections have been fine. No issues there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Same for us. The Salesforce sync is doing what it should.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. So action items: [PERSON_2] and [PERSON_3] send call examples, I take the transfer and handoff issues to the team, and I get [PERSON_4] the pricing breakdown.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That covers it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Great. I'll send a recap this afternoon. Thanks, everyone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks, [PERSON_1].

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Talk soon.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Have a good one.
